markdown_report:
The best early-stage experiment is **shared-weight, context-gated dilation inside corrected NextItNet**. It directly develops the starting idea while preserving one jointly trained network per category. No execution or improvement is claimed.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Different dilation scales expose different temporal offsets. Their usefulness may depend on the current prefix. (2) Sharing convolution weights across scales limits added capacity. It also makes the experiment easier to interpret than adding independently parameterized branches. (3) A gate controls transformations of contextualized states. Neither short dilation nor a small gate guarantees removal of older information.

**Insights from related work.** (1) FADC supplies an adjacent precedent for input-dependent dilation. Its vision setting does not establish recommendation gains. (2) HGNCDSR motivates interest-dependent gating. It does not establish that residual gates forget obsolete interests. (3) R²NS motivates controlling negative difficulty. This is a useful objective-direction alternative, but should remain separate from the architectural experiment.

The conceptual framework separates **accessible evidence** (full prefixes versus explicit windows), **transformation selection** (fixed versus adaptive dilation), and **candidate discrimination** (inherited loss versus additional negatives). These axes organize three directions without confounding their mechanisms.

| Atomic idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Shared-weight dilation gate | 4 | 6 | 6 | 5 | 5 |
| Strict recent-ten windows | 2 | 6 | 6 | 4 | 6 |
| Uniform multi-negative CE | 3 | 6 | 4 | 7 | 4 |

For the gate, the positive/negative assessments are: originality—contextual scale selection/established gating; potential—adaptive history processing/no established generalization gain; user alignment—targets recent-purpose displacement/cannot infer unmet need; model alignment—may reduce contextual confusion/no demonstrated causal diagnosis; difficulty—few added parameters/two convolution evaluations require careful integration. For windows: clear intervention/familiar truncation; useful control/may discard persistent interests; removes distant evidence/recent evidence can still mislead; tests interference/weak attribution; reuses backbone/repeated window computation. For CE: focused discrimination/standard objective; useful optimization control/sampled gains may not transfer; challenges weak alternatives/no direct recency mechanism; addresses margins/training separation may overfit; unchanged inference/careful sampling required.

**Selected mechanism.** Blend complete original- and unit-dilation residual updates using one causal scalar gate per position and block. Initialize toward the original path and retain all inherited training settings. This explicitly targets broad relevance displacing specific recent-purpose matches and isolated older interactions becoming persistent preferences. These remain behavioral hypotheses; compatibility and satisfied demand remain unresolved.

The model-facing target is Industrial_and_Scientific’s 8.04% negative-outranking rate and 0.2551 tenth-percentile margin. Retain fixed diagnostic negatives; cosine-derived scores near 0.5 do not establish dimensional collapse. Compare against the corrected baseline and, budget permitting, a context-independent scalar gate. Select only by unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10; inspect the prescribed twenty users separately.

idea.description: Within each corrected NextItNet residual block, evaluate its complete residual transformation at the inherited dilations and at unit dilation using shared parameters. A causal, position-dependent scalar gate interpolates these transformations before the unchanged identity shortcut is added. Train exactly one network and retain one selected checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: At 10% research progress, a small architectural intervention is preferable to simultaneously changing objectives, context construction and metadata processing. The two explicit user-facing targets are broadly related items displacing specific recent-purpose matches and isolated older interactions being extended into persistent preferences. Adaptive dilation may help distinguish these contexts, but it cannot establish compatibility, replacement need or current intent. The quantitative target is the current Industrial_and_Scientific diagnosis: 8.04% sampled negatives outrank positives, and the tenth-percentile margin is 0.2551. Earlier inspiration metrics describe different runs and must not replace these measurements.
idea.implementation_notes:
This is an integration specification and pseudocode, not a standalone replacement train.py: the supplied prompt does not contain the corrected baseline source. Preserve its actual backbone, sampler, optimizer, loss, initialization, normalization, dropout and checkpoint schedule rather than inventing missing details.

For each residual block, expose its complete residual branch without the shortcut. Evaluate that branch twice with the same learned convolution and normalization parameters: once using every inherited dilation, once replacing temporal dilations with one. Preserve convolution kernel sizes and recompute causal left padding for each dilation. Do not mutate module dilation attributes between forwards; use an explicit dilation argument or functional convolution. If both dilation schedules are identical, evaluate the branch once and omit the redundant gate.

Let h be the block input and r_t the masked causal mean of the original item embeddings over positions max(0,t-4) through t. Compute alpha_t=sigmoid(Linear(concat(h_t,r_t))), with one output channel. Initialize projection weights to zero and bias to -4. Thus alpha initially equals approximately 0.018, making the block close to, but not identical to, the inherited original-dilation block. Use update=(1-alpha)*original_update+alpha*short_update. Add the inherited shortcut and preserve all baseline output processing. The interpolation is over internal transformations, not independently fitted predictors.

Mask padding in the local summary and after baseline operations that can generate padded activations. Preserve tokenwise, sample-independent normalization and original causal ordering. A short branch consumes contextualized h and therefore can carry distant information; neither gate values nor unit dilation demonstrate forgetting. No temporal global pooling, future inputs or cross-example normalization may enter the gate. Preserve inherited dropout placement and disclose that the extra branch changes stochastic draws and optimization trajectories.

Train the gated condition first with inherited objective and sampling. If budget permits, compare a context-independent scalar alpha per block with the same bias initialization; this tests whether contextual modulation adds value beyond static scale interpolation. A separately trained corrected baseline is a control whose predictions are never fused. Do not inspect other trials or reuse their checkpoints. Two shared-weight branch evaluations increase backbone computation despite adding few parameters; actual cost must be measured by the host and charged to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, exactly 200 logical batches per epoch and single-GPU execution. Respect the host SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Preserve splits, evaluator and inherited checkpoint cadence. Selection uses only the arithmetic mean of the four host validation HR@10 values, with 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42.

The predictor writer must embed the identical shared-weight architecture, gate summary width, initialization-independent saved configuration, causal padding and normalization. Each category loads exactly one independently trained selected model/checkpoint. Read the maximum nonpadding positional index for left-padded sequences, never count-1, and preserve the baseline empty-history convention. Keep item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), and ModelView interfaces compatible, with view.model the actual trained nn.Module.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and explicit metric_definitions. The public loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L. Preserve fixed diagnostic negatives and margin definitions. Optional gate summaries must distinguish padding and distinguish gate variability from measured usefulness. Do not claim directional or dimensional collapse from average cosine alone.

Before long training, the host should check future-input perturbation invariance, padding behavior, shared parameter identity across dilation paths, gradient flow through both paths, all-padding handling, and agreement between trained and generated-predictor scores. These are proposed checks, not completed results. Use only public histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions; ratings, reviews, item categories, prices, stores and simulator traits are unavailable. Qualitative follow-up uses the prescribed twenty real training users and separately tracks recent-purpose matches, broad-association displacement, older-interest displacement and indeterminate judgments. No training-margin improvement alone establishes user benefit or full-catalog generalization.
idea.pseudocode:
DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']

# Integrate into the supplied corrected NextItNet; retain its full scaffold.
# This is architecture pseudocode, not a fabricated standalone train.py.

class SharedDilationBlock:
    def forward(self, h, recent_summary, valid):
        original = self.complete_residual_branch(
            h, dilations=self.inherited_dilations)
        if self.inherited_dilations == self.unit_dilations:
            update = original
        else:
            # Same convolution/normalization Parameters, different causal offsets.
            short = self.complete_residual_branch(
                h, dilations=self.unit_dilations)
            alpha = sigmoid(self.scalar_gate(concat(h, recent_summary)))
            update = (1 - alpha) * original + alpha * short
        return inherited_shortcut_add_and_mask(h, update, valid)

# Initialize each nonredundant scalar_gate: weight=0, bias=-4.
# Preserve complete_residual_branch operation order and causal padding.

def log2feats(sequence):
    valid = sequence != 0
    embeddings = item_emb(sequence) * valid[..., None]
    recent = causal_masked_mean(embeddings, valid, width=5)
    h = inherited_input_processing(sequence)
    for block in blocks:
        h = block(h, recent, valid)
    return inherited_output_processing(h)

for category in FOUR_INHERITED_CATEGORY_ROUTES:
    set_training_seed(42)
    model = corrected_nextitnet_with_shared_dilation_blocks(inherited_config)
    for epoch in range(min(inherited_configured_epochs, 200)):
        for batch_index in range(200):
            batch = inherited_family_specific_sample_batch(...)
            inherited_training_step(model, batch)
        inherited_validation_and_checkpoint_selection()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint(category, model, complete_architecture_config)

write_predictor_with_identical_architecture_and_four_category_routing()
# At prediction: gather largest index satisfying sequence[index] != 0.
# Preserve inherited empty-history behavior; load one checkpoint/category.
# Retain ModelView, DiagnosisProbe and diagnostic interpreter contracts.
# Host checks correctness and selects by pinned macro validation HR@10.
# No independent scorer, model averaging, fusion, hidden-test access or extra data.

originality.positive: Combines causal recent-context conditioning with parameter-shared dilation selection inside the required NextItNet backbone.
originality.negative: Dynamic dilation, scalar gates and multiscale residual transformations are established mechanisms; novelty is incremental.

future_potential.positive: Provides a compact experiment distinguishing adaptive temporal transformations from fixed context restrictions and objective changes.
future_potential.negative: Gates may become static, short branches retain contextualized history, and sampled validation gains may not improve current-benefit judgments.

code_difficulty.positive: Adds small scalar projections and reuses the same learned branch parameters without extra datasets or prediction components.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires faithful functional dilation handling, approximately doubled branch computation, padding-safe summaries and identical generated inference code.

related_work.title: FADC: Frequency-Adaptive Dilated Convolution
contributions: Supplied search results describe adapting dilation to local frequency content, providing an adjacent design precedent for input-dependent temporal scale.
limitations: Vision evidence does not establish recommendation gains or causal, padding-safe NextItNet behavior.
The proposed scalar interpolation does not reproduce FADC.

related_work.title: HGNCDSR
contributions: Supplied search results describe feature and instance gates for representing current interests alongside longer-term patterns.
limitations: Does not establish that residual gating removes older information.
Its setting and architecture do not establish effectiveness on the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: R²NS
contributions: Supplied search results describe uniform-negative warm-up and curriculum-controlled sampling hardness across sequential backbones.
limitations: Supports a separate sampling direction rather than validating the selected gate.
Combining sampling changes with the initial gate experiment would weaken attribution.
